newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares hit new highs, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares hit new highs, seen up.

text.p: Leading Russian shares got off to a brisk start on Monday morning as the Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at a new record and traders said the market could rise further on steady demand.
The RTS index opened at a record 363.81 on Monday. It closed at the previous record 362.52 on Friday on a near-record $68.8 million.
"In principle the growth trend remains. It may not be very strong, as the market is a bit speculative, but internal and Western demand is there," said Trinfiko trader Ilya Galtsov.
Traders said the Dow Jones industrial index's Friday slide had not dampened investor enthusiasm for Russian securities, predicting the market would end even higher.
"The market seems to be shrugging off the weakness on Wall Street and heading higher," said Brunswick director Martin Diggle.
"All the fundamental news coming out of Russia is very supportive -- there's a good political climate, steady inflation, and record low T-bill yields. I think we'll see new highs today."
The annualised average yield on Russian treasury bills fell to a record low 26.1 percent on Thursday and Friday and traders said bills would stay at the new level before dropping further.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3230 at 0840 GMT after closing on Friday at $0.3200. Regional electricity utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS slid to $1.353 from $1.364.
Alfa Capital trader Mikhail Khaleyev said the rise could slow later in the day if an early trickle of orders to sell continued.
"(The selling orders) could be partly connected with (the Dow Jones fall) but not just that," Khaleyev said.
